title: Manjari 5. Pilgrimage through Vraja and the Title "Acharya"
html:
Srinivasa with Raghunatha Dasa at Radha-kunda, the circumambulation of Govardhana, Nathji and Vitthalanatha; Varshana, Nandagrama; Jiva and Gopala Bhatta decide to send Srinivasa to Gauda; Srinivasa consents; the Gosvamis give him the title "Acharya" before Govinda; his song on Radha's beauty

[p. 68]

Raga.

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3Thus some time passed;
with Sri Jiva Gosvami (Srinivasa) was always in bliss.

4Meanwhile — the darshana of Sri Radha-kunda
and the meeting with Sri Raghunatha Dasa Gosani.

5Seeing Gosani, Sri Acharya Thakura
offered dandavat obeisances; streams of tears flow from his eyes.

6Gosani raised him and embraced him with love;
his body thrilled, his eyes filled with tears.

7Having asked after his welfare and conversed for some time,
he cooked and that day lay down near (Gosani).

8What unprecedented secret was revealed that night —
the perfection of prema — I cannot write.

9Having stayed awake all night, rising in the morning,
having duly cleaned his teeth, bathed and performed remembrance,

10Gosani, taking Acharya Thakura along,
went ahead to circumambulate Govardhana.

[p. 69]

11Seeing the places of the pastimes, whatever bhavas arose —
telling of all of them, they tasted rasa;

12this is accessible only to experience.
Then they went straight to Nathji.

13Seeing Nathji, in the ocean of bliss
such waves surged up — who could describe them?

14The pujari brought dry prasada,
put garlands on them, applied sandal paste and so on.

15There — the darshana of Vitthalanatha Gosani;
talking of the Beloved (Lord), they rejoiced at heart.1

16From there they came back to the path of the parikrama;
having circumambulated Sri Kunda, they sat down in their lodging.

17Thus for some days he stayed at Sri Kunda
and abundantly received the mercy of Sri Dasa Gosani.

18From there — Varshana, Sanketa-vana;
seeing Nandagrama, his heart was immersed in prema.

19There he saw the king of Vraja and the queen of Vraja,
and between them Krishna and Balarama, givers of all happiness.

20At the darshana of a single place — countless bhavas.
Then he came back to Vrindavana again.

21Bhugarbha Gosani and the other companions of Sri Rupa —
with all of them great prema, joyous talk of Krishna.

22From time to time, coming (to Radha-kunda) and keeping company with Dasa Gosani,
he cannot hold the waves of prema in his body.

[p. 70]

23One day, coming to Sri Bhatta Gosani,
Sri Jiva Gosani explains in detail what is on his mind:

24"Gosani, you know: at the time of my Prabhu's departure
he gave an order — it is always on my mind.

25Whatever order Mahaprabhu gave him,
the same order he gave to me:

26to spread the books of bhakti, Vaishnava conduct,
to establish proper order, all the hidden considerations.

27But I cannot go to another country —
(then) his order would be broken: that I fear.

28Mahaprabhu's birthplace is Sri Gauda-mandala;
there strong bhakti and learning are needed.

29If all these books go to the land of Gauda,
Mahaprabhu's sampradaya will relish them.

30Then all the labour (will be rewarded), the desire fulfilled.
How this can come about I do not see.

31But this Srinivasa Thakura is (fit) in every way:
if at your order he goes to the land of Gauda,

32then all this work will achieve full success:
what would be done through me will be done through him.

33If you yourself tell him very firmly,
then perhaps he will go to his country.

34The burden of fulfilling Sri Gosani-jiu's order —
what shall I say? — see, it all rests on you."

[p. 71]

35Saying this, staying a while longer in joyous talk of Krishna,
he went to his lodging with the devotees.

36The next day Sri Acharya Thakura
came for darshana and bowed down many times;

37and when he had sat down on a seat,
then (Gopala Bhatta) told him all this.

38Hearing it, Acharya Thakura was stunned:
"Prabhu, why do you suddenly say such a thing?

39My desire is to remain in Vrindavana
and serve you with all my heart."

40Bhatta Gosani says: "That is my service —
to go to the land of Gauda and spread the scriptures of bhakti.

41Sri Gosani-jiu's order is to spread bhakti;
I have come to know that it will be done through you.

42There is no doubt of it — I have told you a secret.
If you care for me, you will surely do it."

43Hearing this, Thakura fell silent;
his heart troubled with thoughts, he said nothing.

44Meanwhile Jiva Gosani tells all the mahantas
(to persuade) Srinivasa Thakura to go to Gauda:

45"Finding an occasion, all of you say something to him,
but so that his heart is not displeased."

46Acharya Thakura reflects in his mind:
"The guru's order cannot be transgressed — what can I do?"

[p. 72]

47Whomever he asks, each agrees;
and some lovingly speak even without being asked.

48One day Sri Jiva speaks sweet words:
"Why do I see you so dejected these days?"

49Then Thakura speaks of the sorrow of his heart,
washing his face with tears;

50in a faltering voice he barely utters the sounds —
hearing it, everyone's heart melts:

51"Gosani, I came to understanding in a time of sorrow;
with Mahaprabhu's disappearance it spread everywhere.

52One after another many have vanished;
and those who remain are not aware of themselves.

53Seeing this sorrow, my heart is distraught;
in my mind was living in Vrindavana under Sri Rupa's shelter.

54But they too withdrew (from the manifest world) before (I came);
and still my life has remained — in such misfortune.

55A few of you are (still) here;
if I do not see this, how shall I keep my life?

56But the guru orders me to go to the land of Gauda;
command me what will be for the best."

57Gosani says: "For many days now
I have always wished to send you to the land of Gauda.

58The order that Sri Gosani-jiu gave me,
I know, will be fulfilled through you.

[p. 73]

59Yet I did not speak, fearing your sorrow.
It is fitting to carry out the order for some days.

60The mercy of Sri Gosani-jiu and his associates is upon you;
there will be no obstacles — be sure of it in your heart.

61Having carried out the order in a few days,
what is the difficulty — come back again."

62When Gosani said this so thoroughly,
Thakura's heart softened a little:

63"Your order is my duty;
whether it turns out ill or well — it all rests on you."

64When, saying this, he bowed down,
Gosani, greatly delighted, embraced him.

65The next day, at Govinda's, with Sri Bhatta Gosani
(Jiva) related the whole conversation:

66"I have made him firmly agree;
I do not know what will happen in separation from him."

67Hearing this, Bhatta Gosani felt both joy and grief;
knowing it to be Sri Rupa's will, he took courage.

68(Jiva) says again: "Tomorrow come to Govinda;
giving him the title of Acharya, show mercy."

69Bhatta Gosani says: "As you wish;
I shall certainly come — it is my duty."

70Saying this, both went to their lodgings.
The next day at noon they came and met.

[p. 74]

71Sri Lokanatha Gosani and all the mahantas
were called and told everything in private.

72Hearing it, all were very pleased
and praised them: "You have judged worthily."

73Offering camphor betel, rejoicing,
the adhikari Gosani performed the arati of the rajabhoga.

74Seeing (His) beauty, forgetting themselves right there,
all gaze fixedly at Govinda's face.

75When the arati was over, offering dandavat obeisances,
Sri Jiva Gosvami, taking Thakura by the hand —

76(what) had been agreed with everyone beforehand,
now he only asked permission —

77a pair of fine garments and one shawl
he respectfully put on Thakura,

78brought chatuhsama, the prasada of Sri Govinda,
and marked him with tilaka; cries of "Glory, glory!" arose:

79"From today your title is Acharya,
that you may become the head of many.

80Through you many will be delivered;
there is no doubt of it — a firm judgement."

81Until then he had not been called "Acharya";
today all together gave him this title.2

82Earlier in the book I wrote "Acharya Thakura" here and there
only so that it would be clear who was meant.

[p. 75]

83Sandal paste on his whole body, a prasada garland were given;
gazing at Govinda's face, he floated in bliss.

84At that time Radhika-jiu was not beside (Govinda) —
therefore (Govinda) revealed His longing for Her beauty:

85in private finding Vishakha, the friend of Kishori,
He speaks His heart, knowing her non-different (from Radha).

86In Sri Dasa Gosani's hymn Vishakhananda-da
at the very beginning it is said that she is in essence non-different:

87"She who, by oneness of bhava, name, qualities and so on, is Sri Radhika Herself, the chief beloved of the Moon Krishna — may that Vishakha be gracious."3

88Immersed in this happiness, Acharya Thakura,
at the darshana of Govinda, was filled with boundless prema;

89in that prema he composed an incomparable pada;
as soon as they heard it, all together melted.

90Here is the pada. Raga Suhai. "What carver turned the moon of her face, friend? Who carved her eyes? What happens to my life as I gaze and gaze — only that life itself is witness. Who, cutting jewels with what care, fashioned (the earrings) for her ears? Together with the mind, these five lives (senses), friend, have become yogis rapt in meditation on her. Above her nose shines this 'elephant pearl', set in gold at its side — as if a bud of the moon entwined with lightning were smiling from behind a cloud. On the lovely forehead shines a lovely tilaka, and with it the pattern of her curls; in my heart they glitter, friend, like a row of bees upon the moon. That sway of her braid is Madana's snare, friend — where did she learn it? I have not gazed at her to my heart's fill, friend — that is the great pain of my heart. How sweet her words, one after another, friend — if only I could hold them in my hand! Had the Creator made them so, I would break off piece by piece and eat them. The curve of her arms surpasses a royal elephant's trunk, their tips red as vermilion; the bird of the forest of youth is dying of thirst, friend, begging for the rasa of her touch."4

[p. 76]

91Relishing it, clasping one another's necks, they wept;
whoever saw it knows — who could describe it?

92Acharya Thakura, as was fitting, to all
offers dandavat obeisances, overflowing with prema.

[p. 77]

93Then some embrace him, others bow down;
all bestowed mercy on him, his honour was established.

94Then the adhikari Gosani, Sri Krishna Pandita,
joyfully laid Govinda to rest.

95Afterwards, seating all the mahantas and Vaishnavas,
they partook of prasada in joy.

96To all were given betel, sandal paste and garlands;
then all departed to their lodgings.

97Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

98Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, the fifth manjari, called "The Conferring of the Title of Acharya by the Gosvamis".

Notes

  1. Vitthalanatha (Gusainji), son of Vallabhacharya and head of his sampradaya; Nathji — the Deity Sri Nathji (Gopala) on Govardhana, served by the Vallabhites. Srinivasa's meeting with Vitthalanatha is known only from the Anuraga-valli.
  2. According to the Anuraga-valli, the title "Acharya" was given before Govinda by Jiva with the consent of Gopala Bhatta, Lokanatha and all the mahantas, in connection with Srinivasa's being sent to Gauda. According to the Prema-vilasa (12), Jiva gave the title immediately after the riddle of the trees of Vrindavana was solved (cf. 4.36–54).
  3. Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami's Vishakhananda-da-stotra, 1.
  4. A well-known pada of Srinivasa Acharya ("badana chanda kon kundare kundila go"), included in the pada collections. Govinda's longing for Radha is transcendental prema, not worldly passion; the "five lives" are the five senses.
